notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 11th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 69% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 54:40 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 46:36 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov was added to the roster on Oct 20 and has played beside Kris Letang.

Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

LAK.head: The Kings have a slight edge
LAK.body: Even though Los Angeles will be without Fiala and Pittsburgh gets Solovyov back, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Penguins can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

PIT.head: A slightly uphill night for the Penguins
PIT.body: Even though Pittsburgh gets Solovyov back and Los Angeles will be without Fiala, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. The Penguins’ best way to tip it is piling up shots.

story.head: Kuzmenko returns to Los Angeles
paras: The Penguins (5-7-2) lost 5-4 to Montréal on Oct 31, and the Kings (4-7-2) lost 3-2 to Buffalo the same night. Going in, the Penguins are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 29th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.429) says: their chances are worth about .558, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. So have the Kings (.385 on chances worth .591), where their finishing has held them back.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). As for the Kings, they leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest) and take a lot of low-quality shots (31st). They also lean hard on their top players (3rd lowest), so the Pens roll four lines, but them lean on their top six. The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Kings.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Evgeni Malkin (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 5 A / 13 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Brandt Clarke (3 G / 7 A / 10 P in 13 GP) is next in line.

Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) will likely start for Pittsburgh. Los Angeles has two options in net: Darcy Kuemper (4-3-1 / .878 SV% in 8 GS) and Anton Forsberg (0-4-1 / .902 SV% in 5 GS). Kuemper has started six of their last ten games, but Forsberg got the last one on Oct 31. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: Andrei Kuzmenko faces Los Angeles for the first time since leaving.
The Penguins are newly without Elmer Söderblom, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk and Bryan Rust for several games.
The Kings are newly without Adrian Kempe, have been without Alex Turcotte and Mats Zuccarello for several games, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
Sidney Crosby has four goals in six games against Los Angeles since 2023-24.
